S.FORM: m-angay-ta lu takay mang-anak-u kwan-a ina-na
S.PHON: maŋajta lo takaj maŋanako kwana inana
S.FORM: mangayta lo takay manganako koana inana
S.PHON: maŋajta l[o|u] takaj maŋanak[o|u] k[o|u]ana inana
S.TRANSL: "Let us both go to the field, my child," said his mother.
She went to dig for gold.
She said to the child, "Come here." The mother goes.
The child sees the spirit take the mother up to the sky.
The child sees the spirit take the mother up to the sky.

S.FORM: lavi a nu anak-na s-ina-na k-uli-na
S.PHON: lafi a no anakna ʂinana kolina
S.FORM: lavi a no anakna sinana kolina
S.PHON: lafi a n[o|u] anakna ɕinana k[o|u]lina
S.TRANSL: The child cries, "Mother, return!"
"Where is your mother?" said his father.
"Mother isn't here," he replied.
"The spirit crept up and flew away with Mother."

S.FORM: mang-ep su aru nu vařit s-ama-na kavangepna?
S.PHON: maŋəp ʂo aɻo no fa*it ʂamana kafaŋəpnaʔ
S.FORM: mangep so aro no vazit samana kavangepna
S.PHON: maŋəp ʂ[o|u] aɻ[o|u] n[o|u] farit ʂamana kafaŋəpna
S.TRANSL: The father took many strips of bamboo,

S.FORM: mang-ep su aru nu yaked s-ama-na kavangepna?
S.PHON: maŋəp ʂo aɻo no jakəɖ ʂamana kafaŋəpnaʔ
S.FORM: mangep so aro no yaked samana kavangepna
S.PHON: maŋəp ʂ[o|u] aɻ[o|u] n[o|u] jakəɖ ʂamana kafaŋəpna
S.TRANSL: The father took many strips of bamboo,

S.FORM: k-angay-na lu tatala katukad-na lu kwang
S.PHON: kaŋajna lo tatala katokaɖna lo kwaŋ
S.FORM: kangayna lo tatala katokadna lo koang
S.PHON: kaŋajna l[o|u] tatala kat[o|u]kaɖna l[o|u] k[o|u]aŋ
S.TRANSL: went to the boat, and sailed far away.

S.FORM: m-angay lu ilaud m-angay lu vaǥay nu kwaway
S.PHON: maŋaj lo ilaoɖ maŋaj lo faɰaj no kwawaj
S.FORM: mangay lo ilaod mangay lo vahay no koaway
S.PHON: maŋaj l[o|u] ila[o|u]ɖ maŋaj l[o|u] faɰaj n[o|u] k[o|u]awaj
S.TRANSL: They went to a foreign country to the spirit's house.

S.FORM: lu kwang chita-en-a u aru nu tau
S.PHON: lo kwaŋ ʨitaəna o aɻo no tao
S.FORM: lo koang citaena o aro no tao
S.PHON: l[o|u] k[o|u]aŋ ʨitaəna [o|u] aɻ[o|u] n[o|u] ta[o|u]
S.TRANSL: Far away, they saw many people.
They saw his house in the foreign country.
"You go home to your own people,"

S.FORM: kwan-a kařwan nu tau lu ilaud
S.PHON: kwana ka*wan no tao lo ilaoɖ
S.FORM: koana kadoan no tao lo ilaod
S.PHON: k[o|u]ana kaɖ[o|u]an n[o|u] ta[o|u] l[o|u] ila[o|u]ɖ
S.TRANSL: said the foreigner.

S.FORM: ku-mi-chita-en nu mavakes-ku naket-na nu kwaway
S.PHON: komiʨitaən no mafakəʂko nakətna no kwawaj
S.FORM: komicitaen no mavakesko naketna no koaway
S.PHON: k[o|u]miʨitaən n[o|u] mafakəʂk[o|u] nakətna n[o|u] k[o|u]awaj
S.TRANSL: "I see the spirit captured my wife."

S.FORM: m-angay-ka lu makarang nu tukun kwan-a nu tau
S.PHON: maŋajka lo makaɻaŋ no tokon kwana no tao
S.FORM: mangayka lo makarang no tokon koana no tao
S.PHON: maŋajka l[o|u] makaɻaŋ n[o|u] t[o|u]k[o|u]n k[o|u]ana n[o|u] ta[o|u]
S.TRANSL: "You go to the stilt house on the mountain," the foreigner said,
"and see there how your wife is being cared for."
"Who are you coming here to look for your mother?

S.FORM: nak-nakem-ku-inyu? anak nu yamen lu yami
S.PHON: naknakəmkoinjoʔ anak no jamən lo jami
S.FORM: naknakemkoinio anak no yamen lo yami
S.PHON: naknakəmk[o|u]ini[o|u] anak n[o|u] jamən l[o|u] jami
S.TRANSL: I think that you are a child of us Yami people.
I wonder if you are really our child, dear.
If I wash

S.FORM: su pasavuřen-ku chinwan nu maumlesan su chinwat-an
S.PHON: ʂo paʂafo*ənko ʨinwan no maomləʂan ʂo ʨinwatan
S.FORM: so pasavořenko cinoan no maomlesan so cinoatan
S.PHON: ʂ[o|u] paʂaf[o|u]*ənk[o|u] ʨin[o|u]an n[o|u] ma[o|u]mləʂan ʂ[o|u] ʨin[o|u]atan
S.TRANSL: you with boiling water
and your skin peels off,
then you are not our child."
She washed him and the child was fine, so she said, "You are really our child."
The spirit's wing was burned.
"Let's go and see them catching fish."
She made a hat, and went

S.FORM: nu vaǥay-na nu apia nu k-anak-an
S.PHON: no faɰajna no apia no kanakan
S.FORM: no vahayna no apia no kanakan
S.PHON: n[o|u] faɰajna n[o|u] apia n[o|u] kanakan
S.TRANSL: to the child's good house.
"You are going, dear child," said his mother.

S.FORM: m-angay-ka chyaa? nu apia tau kwan
S.PHON: maŋajka ʨjaaʔ no apia tao kwan
S.FORM: mangayka ciaa no apia tao koan
S.PHON: maŋajka ʨiaa n[o|u] apia ta[o|u] k[o|u]an
S.TRANSL: It doesn't matter if you do go. They are good people over there.

S.FORM: apia nun m-angay-ku-rana kwan m-angay kalilyan u vaunda
S.PHON: apia non maŋajkoɻana kwan maŋaj kaliljan o faonɖa
S.FORM: apia non mangaykorana koan mangay kalilian o vaonda
S.PHON: apia n[o|u]n maŋajk[o|u]ɻana k[o|u]an maŋaj kalilian [o|u] fa[o|u]nɖa
S.TRANSL: "Yes, good people; so I'll go," he said, and went to the plain (where the mother had been taken up).
The child cries, "You are so very tall.
I'm afraid, because I'm just little."
"Come here, dear little one."
"I don't want to; I am not going, because Mother will scold us.

S.FORM: y-abu m-angay-ku mwama tu kungyan avay-aken ina
S.PHON: jabo maŋajko mwama to koŋjan afajakən ina
S.FORM: yabo mangayko moama to kongian avayaken ina
S.PHON: jab[o|u] maŋajk[o|u] m[o|u]ama t[o|u] k[o|u]ŋian afajakən ina
S.TRANSL: I'm not going to do planting in the mountains. Mother will scold me.
I'm going to look for something here in the trees."
"Come here, dear."
"I don't want to," he said.
"Then I'll cut off your mother's head. That's why I'm going."
"I don't want you to. I musn't let mother's head be cut off.
Cut off a goat's head."
"Come here, dear.
I'm going to cut off your mother's head."
"Yes," and the child began to cry.
After five days, he cut off her head.
After five days, he cut off her head.
She couldn't move
or bear children any more.
The husband wailed,
and cried, "Your mother's blood is flowing down.
Don't bury her."
They went home and combed their hair
and prepared the vegetables
while the husband cried.
He saw the mother's spirit, and she said, "You were not bad.
My head was cut off and are you crying?
Look at me." "Let us both go,"
said her husband.
"Excuse me, Machinara, I'm going to sit by our betel nut basket.
